headline: High: Chatwoot’s broad network egress plus customer-data handling can leak or misroute sensitive support content, while LightZero’s no-IO profile limits direct interaction risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between Chatwoot and LightZero. Chatwoot has broad network egress, but LightZero has no browser, MCP, filesystem, or subprocess surfaces, so there is no plausible default path for Chatwoot content to be parsed as instructions by LightZero.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Chatwoot output into a LightZero prompt or config, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added later, the pathway should be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workflows with no copy-paste bridge.
Disable any future shared queue or clipboard integration.
Review any manual handoff text before reuse.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, messages, and reports, but LightZero is local-only with no network egress or filesystem read/write. The pair does not show a shared workspace or outbound path from LightZero, so leakage risk is limited unless operators bridge data manually.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports customer records into a shared folder, leakage risk increases.
IF LightZero is wrapped by another service that adds network egress, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Keep customer data out of shared directories.
Use separate service accounts and credentials.
Redact support transcripts before any manual transfer.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on Chatwoot exports.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress, but LightZero explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, or use MCP. There is no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface in the profiles, so a capability conflict is not plausible by default.
conditions: IF LightZero is deployed behind an external orchestrator that grants shared writes, conflict risk should be rechecked.
IF both agents are later given access to the same mutable API scope, reassess.
mitigations: Keep LightZero read-only as profiled.
Avoid granting Chatwoot write access to LightZero-managed resources.
Separate deployment credentials.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can emit support content and reports, but LightZero is a game-playing system with no documented action-taking authority. Without evidence that LightZero consumes Chatwoot outputs as authoritative inputs, the cascade is mainly a manual workflow risk rather than an automated failure path.
conditions: IF an operator feeds Chatwoot-generated text into LightZero as authoritative state, cascading errors become more likely.
IF LightZero is extended to act on Chatwoot outputs automatically, reassess severity.
mitigations: Require human review before reusing Chatwoot outputs.
Separate support summaries from game-state inputs.
Label any transferred text as untrusted.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and messages, which can include regulated personal data, while LightZero touches no data classes and has no residency or retention controls documented. The mismatch is not a direct violation by itself, but Chatwoot’s support-data handling creates compliance exposure if routed into an environment without matching controls.
conditions: IF customer messages contain regulated personal data and are exported into LightZero-related logs, compliance risk increases.
IF Chatwoot is configured for a jurisdiction with stricter retention than the downstream workflow, reassess.
mitigations: Keep regulated support data out of LightZero workflows.
Minimize retention of exported transcripts.
Review jurisdictional handling for customer records.
requires-engineering: document data-flow and retention boundaries.
